content:
Priya (prodeng): heads up — noticed telemetry dashboard showing rows from other orgs when using the delegated view role after last nights' rollout. reproducer below, visible in canary and a handful of prod users.
Mike S: ugh, can you paste the minimal repro?
Priya (prodeng): steps: 1) login as a user with 'view:delegated' on org A 2) open /console/insights/telemetry 3) filters show data rows from org B intermittently. happens on rapid org-switch.
Tara (eng-platform): is this console-only or does the backend API return mixed rows?
Priya (prodeng): initial check shows backend /internal/insights/query returns correct org-scoped results when called with X-Redwood-Org header, but console prefetch + cached route sometimes injects stale orgid into the final query.
Nora R: do we have an edge or proxy layer that rewrites org headers on fast nav? saw similar in session-proxy bug months ago.
Dan L: paging @infra-bot for recent deploys/rollouts that touched prefetch/caching.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollout 2026-03-19T02:12:33Z applied to console-prefetch v2 -> instances: console-canary-1, console-frontend-7. No DB migrations.
Mike S: so likely this is a client-side prefetch cache key collision or affinity tag leak, not backend query auth. Priya, can you dump the console prefetch log when repro'd?
Priya (prodeng): pasted snippet: ```INFO prefetchtask=ui-prefetch key=workspace:insights:user-42:org-NULL result=hit source=memorycache``` then later ```INFO render query org=org-A final_query_org=org-B```
Tara (eng-platform): that pattern looks like the cache key lost org scoping (org-NULL). maybe we introduced a fast-path that omits org for unauthenticated prefetch and then stitches user org later — race window.
Nora R: If prefetch inserts partial payload into the UI state and we then hydrate with user org info, race could cause mixing. This is a multi-tenant isolation bug. We should assume worst-case and act fast.
Dan L: quick mitigation: flip prefetch to strict mode (reject/skip cache entries that don't include org header) and roll back the fast-path. I can push a kill-switch flag to canary.
Mike S: agree. Also we should add a gateway invariant: strip any upstream X-Redwood-Org header coming from client and only allow internal services to set it. prevents header spoofing. But primary fix belongs in console prefetch keying.
Priya (prodeng): deploying kill-switch to canary now: config set console.prefetch.strict_org=true. Will monitor.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: config change applied to console-canary-1 at 1876543301.
Tara (eng-platform): create an alert to catch any cross-org rows in dashboards — add sampling rule to telemetry that flags rows where event.org != request.auth_org. we can detect scope drifts quickly.
Nora R: already opened a quick eval: eval-id 2026-03-prefetch-telemetry-leak. hooking into alerts.
Mike S: longer term: 1) fix cache key to include org id always; 2) audit every prefetch path for missing auth scoping; 3) add unit/integration tests that fuzz rapid org-switch; 4) add a canary rollout that keeps old path on 10% traffic.
Dan L: + add a console-side guard that refuses to hydrate prefetched data when the cached item org != current auth org. Fail closed.
Priya (prodeng): we're seeing canary with strict_org enabled: so far zero reproductions for 30m. canary traffic ~1.2k requests.
Mike S: good. assign an owner for the fix PR? Tara take it and pair with Nora for tests.
Tara (eng-platform): will do. opening PR w/ branch name: fix/prefetch-org-key-18765. will include test harness and telemetry alert.
Nora R: also bouncing an RFC about where scoping invariants should live — gateway vs console vs service. my take: defensive layering. every layer validates. but ownership for this bug: console prefetch.
Priya (prodeng): decision notes: immediate rollback not needed because kill-switch works. next steps tracked in GH issue #3842. tagging SRE for postmortem if we see any production leaks.
Dan L: thanks all. follow-up: schedule a short post-mortem + timeline to backfill tests.
Mike S: thanks — @Priya please post a short summary in #incidents if the alert fires or if we find any leaked PII. :thumbsup:
Priya (prodeng): will do. updating #incidents if anything new.
